messages:
maria.rev: Copperline wants to replace CompetitorX with Redwood. POC asks: drop-in shim, billing equivalence (they bill per-bucket), security questionnaire, and any response deltas that break their scoring. Can presales ops?
ajay.se: I can own the adapter. Will preserve endpoint shape and translate to /v1/completions. Main risk: tokenization differences and stop-sequence semantics.
tess.eng: Quick notes: tokenization typically shifts output length +/- 5-12 tokens; sampling defaults differ (temp/top_p) which changes outputs; exact-stop matching can be off if competitor used raw "\n\n". We should include normalization in shim.
olivia.solutions: I'll build a parity suite: 200 prompts across classification, summarization, extraction. Run A/B and surface major regression rate. Also add a small cost estimator: sample their responses to map buckets -> avg tokens.
neil.security: Security asks: SCIM + SSO, BYOK (AWS/GCP KMS), audit log export, EU residency. We'll need contact for SOC2 addendum and ACLs.
ajay.se: Adapter snippet for common call:
```
POST /v1/bridge/respond
{ "prompt": "...", "max_out": 64 }
```
Translate to Redwood:
```
POST /v1/completions
{ "model":"redwood-gen","input":"...","max_output_tokens":64 }
```
maria.rev: Acceptance criteria suggestion: parity suite <=3% major regressions; P95 latency <700ms at their expected load (100 TPS); billing projection within 12% after sampling; security questionnaire signed.
olivia.solutions: Timeline: Day 0-2 creds + security kickoff; Day 3-5 build adapter + smoke; Day 6-8 run parity & cost sampling; Day 9 demo.
tess.eng: Engineering caveat: if their scoring relies on exact character offsets, tokenization diffs may break it. We can add an offset-mapping heuristic in adapter but document limitations.
neil.security: I'll start the SA doc and request their compliance contact.
ajay.se: I'll open the proxy repo and post smoke logs here by EOD tomorrow.
maria.rev: Thanks team. Keeping this thread for all POC coordination. :thumbsup:
